## Description

`\X2\HHHH…\X0\` carries one or more 4-hex-digit UCS-2 code units. The closing `\X0\` is mandatory and the hex run length must be a multiple of four. Real-world defects: missing `\X0\` before the closing apostrophe, three-digit groups (`\X2\03B\X0\`), embedded whitespace splitting the hex run, nested `\X2\` opened without closing the prior, and folding the closing apostrophe into the hex run.

## Reproducer recipe

`#1=PERSON('\X2\03B\X0\');` (3 hex digits); `'name=\X2\30A2'` (no `\X0\`); `'name=\X2\30A2 30A4\X0\rest'` (whitespace split); `'name=\X2\30A2\X2\30A4\X0\'` (nested without close).

## Expected kernel behavior

validate group count and codepoint range; emit `E_BAD_X2_DIRECTIVE` on malformed input; warn-and-best-effort decode the chars present without crashing.

**Structured outcomes** (extracted from prose; for downstream auto-grading):
- disallowed: `crash`

Crash potential when an out-of-range value is fed to a downstream UTF-8 encoder.
